headline: China's army has opened new military colleges to train specialists in unmanned systems and AI, and officers to inspect discipline.
score_reason: Lowered 1 from 5: the colleges opened on 30 Sep 2026 (before 2 Oct) and only a short relay of the SCMP report could be read.
importance_line: It signals more training in unmanned systems and AI for China's armed forces, which matters to the PLA's future technical staff and to governments watching its build-up; the relay gives no course sizes or content, and the SCMP original could not be checked.
summary: UA.News, summarising a South China Morning Post report, says that on 30 Sep 2026 a PLA university set up a College of Unmanned and Intelligent Engineering and two colleges for non-commissioned officers, while the National Defence University opened a College of Discipline Inspection, Law and Politics. It adds that the discipline college opened amid a large anti-corruption campaign in the army in which many senior commanders have been removed.
notes: Original outlet South China Morning Post (blocked, 403). Written from the UA.News summary of the SCMP report. The 30 Sep date is calculated from 'on Wednesday'.
